findings.claim: Acceptance task 5 ('Re-run the eval against the reviewed truth with the new corpus shape; record the post-change baseline and any metric movement') is marked complete ([x]) but was never performed — the truth is still draft, the run is recorded BLOCKED, and the regression-test 'pass' compares unchanged results/ against an unchanged baseline, so it proves nothing about the new corpus shape.
findings.evidence: EVAL-RESULTS.md: 'Live re-run of the 24 items against the new corpus shape | **BLOCKED** — ground truth is still `draft: 24, reviewed: 0`'; metrics-summary.json post_change_baseline status 'blocked', metric_movement null; verification.md acceptance criterion: 'The eval regression test passes against the reviewed truth with the new corpus shape, and any metric change is recorded rather than tuned away'; tasks.json header shows '- [x] 5'. The declared dependency change-rah-007 ('operator review ... has not landed') is itself incomplete, so the change is certifying against an unmet dependency.
findings.suggested_fix: Un-check task 5 and record the change verdict as BLOCKED per the provenance enum until rah-007 task 2 lands, then regenerate baseline-snapshot.json from reviewed truth, re-run with normalized corpora, and record real metric movement.

findings.claim: The new path-traversal guard validates artifact_id and concept_id but leaves GOAL_ID as an unchecked path component, so `--goal-id ../../outside` still escapes the artifact store even though the spec scenario promises the script 'writes nothing outside the goal's artifact store'.
findings.evidence: The new case statements check only `$ARTIFACT_ID/$CONCEPT_ID` and `$ARTIFACT_ID$CONCEPT_ID`; ARTIFACTS_DIR is then built as `"${LEARN_HOME}/goals/${GOAL_ID}/artifacts/${CONCEPT_ID}"` with GOAL_ID interpolated raw, and `mkdir -p` will happily create `goals/../../outside/...`. The integration test only probes concept_id traversal ('../escape'), never goal_id.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply the same separator/dot-segment case check to GOAL_ID before constructing ARTIFACTS_DIR, and add a test assertion that a traversal goal_id is refused.

findings.claim: learn-grade Step 1 instructs the grader to derive key_points/misconceptions itself for 1.0.0 corpora ('derive them the same way before grading'), directly contradicting the spec authored in this same change that mandates '--normalize ... never by a second derivation'.
findings.evidence: learn-grade/SKILL.md hunk: 'A corpus whose sources lack either field is an older shape (`schema_version` 1.0.0): derive them the same way before grading and note it in the grade narrative.' vs openspec/specs/learn-model-coherence/spec.md: 'A corpus at the older shape SHALL be brought to this shape by the same script's `--normalize` mode, never by a second derivation.' HARNESS.md correctly routes through --normalize, so the two docs in the same diff disagree.
findings.suggested_fix: Change Step 1 to direct the grader to run `content-grounding-kb.sh --normalize <corpus> --output <tmp>` and grade against the normalized file, matching HARNESS.md and the spec.

findings.claim: The 'no skill still documents the old flat or hyphenated artifact paths' gate uses an unquoted `--include=*.sh`, which glob-expands in the caller's cwd (repo root contains install.sh), silently narrowing the grep to files named install.sh and skipping every real .sh file whenever the test is run from a directory containing any .sh file.
findings.evidence: `bash -c '! grep -rn "..." "$1/skills/learn" --include=SKILL.md --include=*.sh --exclude-dir=tests'` — `*.sh` is unquoted inside the bash -c string and expands against the process cwd, not $ROOT; from repo root it becomes `--include=install.sh`, making the .sh half of the gate vacuous.
findings.suggested_fix: Quote the pattern: `--include='*.sh'` (or pass it as an argument), and add a positive control proving write-artifact.sh was actually scanned.

findings.claim: The wrapper execs `bash` from PATH, so the test's '/bin/bash 3.2' parity run re-dispatches the shared script to whatever bash is first on PATH — the spec scenario 'byte-identical output, under /bin/bash 3.2 as well' and constraint C-05's '/bin/bash script.sh' testing rule are not actually exercised for the shared script.
findings.evidence: Wrapper: `exec bash "${_root}/shared/scripts/content-grounding-kb.sh" "$@"`; test: `check "wrapper resolves under /bin/bash 3.2" /bin/bash "$WRAP_KB" ...` — only the 16-line wrapper runs under /bin/bash; the shared script (all the real logic) runs under PATH bash.
findings.suggested_fix: Exec with the same interpreter that invoked the wrapper (e.g. `exec /bin/bash ...` or re-exec via "$BASH"), or have the test invoke the shared script directly under /bin/bash.

findings.claim: The test asserts write-artifact.sh stdout contains `.concept_id == "c1"`, but the script's documented success contract is `{"ok":true,"path":"..."}` and no hunk in this diff adds concept_id to the success output; if the unchanged tail prints only ok+path, the new integration gate fails as written.
findings.evidence: Test: `check "write-artifact.sh exits ok" jq -e '.ok == true and .concept_id == "c1"' <<<"$OUT1"`; write-artifact.sh header (both old and new): '# Exits 0 and prints {"ok":true,"path":"..."} on success.' — the diff's last hunk ends at `mkdir -p "$ARTIFACTS_DIR"` with no change to the success print.
findings.suggested_fix: Either emit concept_id in the success JSON and update the header comment, or relax the assertion to ok+path and derive concept_id from the path.

findings.claim: The 'authored key_points kept verbatim' normalize check is order-dependent and vacuous at N=0: it compares the authored-only subset of the original against the first N key_points of the normalized corpus (where every source now has key_points), which only holds if the authored sources happen to lead the array, and trivially passes ([] == []) when the eval corpus has no authored key_points at all.
findings.evidence: `diff <(jq -c '[.sources[] | select(has("key_points")) | .key_points]' $EVAL_CORPUS) <(jq -c '[.sources[] | select(.key_points != null) | .key_points] | .[0:($2|tonumber)]' normalized.json)` — after normalization all 12 sources satisfy `.key_points != null`, so the slice assumes positional alignment that nothing guarantees.
findings.suggested_fix: Join on source_ref: compare `.sources[] | select(has("key_points")) | {source_ref, key_points}` between original and normalized sorted by source_ref, and fail if the count is zero so the check is never vacuous.

findings.claim: The spec asserts present-tense SHALLs for behavior owned by change-rah-009 (add_gap/add_session/resolve_gap persistence, fifth-observation mastery, FSRS difficulty, learn-practice calling add_session), but rah-009 is not a declared dependency of this change (deps: rah-005, rah-007) and learn-practice is not touched in this diff, so the 'current truth' spec may describe unlanded behavior.
findings.evidence: spec.md 'Skills call the write paths' requires learn-practice to name add_session — no learn-practice file appears in the diff; acceptance criteria 'Depends on: change-rah-007-eval-ground-truth-review, change-rah-005-claim-labels-and-provenance' (no rah-009); verification.md says 'openspec validate passes with both new capabilities' while this diff adds only one spec.
findings.suggested_fix: Either sequence this change after rah-009 (add the dependency), or mark the rah-009-owned requirements as delta/pending until that change lands.

findings.claim: subject_to_slug now has two implementations (sourced lib/slug.sh when present, inline fallback otherwise), so the same input can produce different corpus_id slugs between a repo checkout and an installed layout that ships the script without lib/, undermining the 'one grounding script' byte-parity goal across environments.
findings.evidence: `if [ -f "$_slug_lib" ]; then . "$_slug_lib" else subject_to_slug() { ... sed 's/[^a-z0-9]\{1,\}/-/g' ... } fi` — the inline fallback even uses a different sed expression than the pre-change inline version (`\+` → `\{1,\}`), showing the two paths can drift.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the wrapper/test assert the lib and fallback produce identical slugs for a probe string, or fail loudly when the lib is expected but absent.
